articles.title: HOW FAIRE DEVELOPED PRODUCT BUILDERS
articles.summary: Faire accelerated product development by transforming engineers into "product builders," combining coding with product and design thinking. This shift allowed engineers to manage features end-to-end, reducing dependencies on PMs and designers, freeing them to focus on complex customer problems. Early results showed significant improvement in engineers' contributions to customer outcomes, with a notable increase in product and design thinking capabilities.

articles.title: RISING HEALTH INSURANCE PREMIUMS SQUEEZE PAYCHECKS IN 2026
articles.summary: Employers are paying more for health coverage while employees are feeling the squeeze. Total family premiums rose 9.8% from 2025 to 2026, while gross pay for the same employees grew 6.4%. Employers still pay most of the premium. More employees are on high-deductible plans, with the share of family enrollees on HSA-eligible plans rising from 20.9% in 2021 to 33.9% in 2026.

articles.title: INSIDE CLAY'S GTM MACHINE
articles.summary: Build your account scoring around what your highest-paying customers have in common. Clay's head of GTM engineering found that its top customers by ARR had at least 10% of their employees in sales or go-to-market roles. That pattern became one input in its fit score for other accounts. The fit score feeds a weekly ranking that gives each rep five accounts from their own book to focus on.

articles.title: THE SECRET BEHIND VIRAL PRODUCT LAUNCHES
articles.summary: Startups have the unique opportunity to capture millions of eyeballs and attention worth millions of dollars on X. This post looks at how to actually win the timeline for a day. It provides clear steps to follow to grab attention, even against AI, which has industrialized content production and saturated the space. It also covers the different things a company must do to coordinate a launch with over a million views.

articles.title: SHOULD YOU INCORPORATE AI IN YOUR POSITIONING?
articles.summary: A homepage that sounds like your closest competitor's feels like a positioning failure. A positioning consultant argues that this can be the right call for AI CRMs such as Lightfield and Day AI, which have both used "AI-native CRM." A buyer using Salesforce or HubSpot first needs a reason to consider switching to an AI CRM. The differences between the startups can wait for a sales conversation once that buyer is ready to try one.

articles.title: THE THING I TALK TO MOST
articles.summary: Picnic's founder had an agent read customer replies and come back with a feature he hadn't thought to build. One person wanted to stop approving each inbox search, and another needed to keep a client's Social Security numbers out of the results. The agent proposed a permission that stays on until revoked and lets the customer block specific terms. It suggested showing the idea first to the person with the privacy request and drafted a reply.

articles.title: THE GREAT SOFTWARE IP WRITEDOWN
articles.summary: Software companies count on years of engineering work continuing to pay off after the product ships. Faster copying is turning that investment into a recurring expense. Agents can already start reproducing apps from screenshots. Switching is now easier too because an agent can pull customer records out of the old web app even when the vendor offers no clean export.
